phases.message: I'm Lucia, trade compliance at Ashby Kitchenworks. Start in Ledgerline: read the product master and the duty we paid on every entry since May last year.
Docshelf has our product specifications, our CBP ruling and the tariff extracts. Read them all, and work out how each product should be classified.

Forwarden is our customs broker. Read our entries, how each was classified and liquidated, and the broker's notes. Have Forwarden correct every entry that was misclassified and can still be corrected before liquidation, for the right duty.

Portline Entries is our trade account with CBP. Read the rules, the liquidations and our protests, and protest every liquidated entry we can still protest that was misclassified, for the right refund. Don't protest anything that was right, or that can't be protested yet or any more. Then tell me what you filed, what's due next and what you left alone and why.

documents.title: New York ruling NY N998214 to Ashby Kitchenworks, 12 March 2024
documents.text: U.S. Customs and Border Protection, New York ruling NY N998214, issued to Ashby Kitchenworks Inc. on 12 March 2024 under 19 CFR Part 177. Merchandise: MP-30, two oval melamine platters for serving food. The applicable subheading is 3924.10.2000, HTSUS, which provides for tableware and kitchenware of plastics: plates, cups, saucers, soup bowls, cereal bowls, sugar bowls, creamers, gravy boats, serving dishes and platters. The rate of duty is 6.5% ad valorem. This ruling is issued under 19 CFR Part 177 and should be attached to the entry documents.

documents.title: HTSUS 2026, headings 3924 and 3926, and the General Rules of Interpretation
documents.text: From the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (2026), column 1 general rates. 3924: Tableware, kitchenware, other household articles and hygienic or toilet articles, of plastics: 3924.10 Tableware and kitchenware: 3924.10.10 salt, pepper, mustard and ketchup dispensers, 3.4%; 3924.10.20 plates, cups, saucers, soup bowls, cereal bowls, sugar bowls, creamers, gravy boats, serving dishes and platters, 6.5%; 3924.10.30 trays, 5.3%; 3924.10.40 other, 3.4%. 3926: Other articles of plastics: 3926.90.99 other, 5.3%. GRI 1: classification is determined by the terms of the headings and any relative section or chapter notes. GRI 3(a): the heading with the most specific description is preferred. Chapter 39, note 1: 'plastics' means the materials of headings 3901 to 3914, which include the silicones of heading 3910, so articles of silicone are articles of plastics.

broker_notes.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Forwarden's notes for Ashby Kitchenworks. Topics: classification, psc.

Our classification database held SP-12 under 3926.90.99 and BM-40 under 3924.10.20 from its set-up in April 2025 until Friday 14 August 2026, when we corrected both to 3924.10.40 to match Ashby's product master. Entries we filed before 14 August used the old numbers; entries filed after it use 3924.10.40. MP-30 has always been entered under 3924.10.20, as Ashby's ruling NY N998214 says, with the ruling attached.

A post-summary correction (PSC) corrects an entry summary CBP has accepted and that is not yet liquidated. Under CBP's test in force (19 CFR 101.9(b); 91 FR 41053, 6 July 2026), it must be transmitted within 300 days of the date of entry or up to 15 days before the scheduled liquidation date, whichever is earlier. Once an entry is liquidated, it can be corrected only by a protest (or a prior disclosure). An entry past its PSC window but not yet liquidated waits for liquidation, and is then protested. We transmit a PSC the day you instruct it.

cbp_rules.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. CBP's rules on liquidation, protests, post-summary corrections, rulings and refunds, as they stand on that date. Topics: liquidation, protest, psc, rulings, refunds.

Liquidation is CBP's final computation of the duty on an entry. An entry not liquidated within one year of the date of entry is deemed liquidated at the rate and amount the importer asserted (19 U.S.C. 1504(a); 19 CFR 159.11). In CBP's normal practice an entry that needs no review is scheduled to liquidate about 314 days after entry, on a Friday, and Portline shows the date.

19 U.S.C. 1514 and 19 CFR Part 174: the classification and rate and amount of duties, and the liquidation of an entry, are final unless protested. The importer of record (or its surety, or its authorized agent) may protest. A protest must be filed within 180 days after, but not before, the date of liquidation (1514(c)(3); 174.12(e)): a protest of an unliquidated entry is not accepted. It states the entry number and date, the liquidation date, the merchandise, and the nature of and reasons for the objection (174.13). CBP decides it within 2 years (174.21).

A post-summary correction is filed by the entry's filer, before liquidation only, within 300 days of the date of entry or up to 15 days before the scheduled liquidation date, whichever is earlier (CBP's PSC test under 19 CFR 101.9(b), 91 FR 41053). After that, an unliquidated entry is corrected by protest once it liquidates.

19 CFR 177.9: a ruling letter is binding on CBP for the transaction it describes, and a classification ruling applies to merchandise identical to the description in the ruling, until it is modified or revoked. An entry of that merchandise under the ruling's subheading is correctly classified.

When a protest is allowed or a PSC is accepted, CBP reliquidates or liquidates the entry at the corrected rate and refunds the excess duty deposited, with interest from the date of deposit (19 U.S.C. 1505(b) and (c)).
